parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Around 10 years ago, Australia Zoo, the University of Queensland and Queensland Parks and Wildlife, undertook a project to monitor the movements and behaviour of the crocodiles in Lakefield National Park. The aim of the study was to provide better information on how adult crocodiles there interact within a river system, enabling people to make better decisions on how to manage crocodile populations. This project can lead the world in crocodile management because of the use of satellites, which enables scientists to stably receive accurate information being sent back to them on the computer. Even though the crocodiles can travel very long distances, scientists can still know where they are and study their habits. The study is going to help scientists gain further knowledge on crocodile behaviour, which can help make informed decisions on the management plans for crocodiles not only in Australia but around the world.
Crocodile tracking isn't a new idea. In Australia, crocodile studies have been previously conducted by radio. A miniature electronic device was implanted under the skin of these animals and they were released back into the river. These tags enabled scientists to track the movements of these particular crocodiles over the next 10 years. Of course, there are some unexpected challenges. The data transmitted from each receiver is recorded by some devices employed in the receiving stations. However, some devices are too old that they always lose signals due to a variety of reasons. So they can't track those animals which they have been studying for months. In order to study the crocodiles, they must first be captured so that the device can be put on them. But this is a very difficult task because they are alert and afraid of being followed by humans. So it might take the team several hours to capture one. The tracking device has signal transmitters inside and it's waterproof. It is attached to the head of the crocodile, so the crocodile cannot remove the device with its feet or tail.
The research has begun to reveal the movements of crocodiles. Data showed that crocodiles tend to be more active at night time. The GPS sometimes shows that in some areas the crocodiles are overpopulated. So scientists at the park have to use a helicopter to relocate the crocodiles in order to control their population in the area. A crocodile would be taken many kilometers away from its original place. However, scientists found that the relocation methods were ineffective because the relocated crocodiles will return to their original location following the most direct route within one week. The tracking data shows that the crocodiles swim right back to where they came from when moved. Crocodiles sometimes travel hundreds of kilometers from Indonesia to Australia in order to reproduce. It is interesting to see that they can always find their way and they will not get lost in the ocean. Scientists realized that crocodiles are able to navigate. This is an important ability for them when they have to migrate for very long distances. We may wonder if human beings can learn from the crocodiles and find our way without using technology. However, through lots of research and experiments, scientists conclude that crocodiles can tell directions by using their senses to the sun so that they know where they are going. This is an ability which human beings don't possess. Another finding is that, like the migration of birds who can travel thousands and thousands of kilometers, crocodiles have the same system to help them travel. The research is still going on in Northern Australia. Scientists are working hard to gather more information about this amazing creature.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到这项研究能世界领先，是因为使用了卫星（satellites）技术，这能让科学家稳定接收准确信息。
This project can lead the world in crocodile management because of the use of satellites, which enables scientists to stably receive accurate information being sent back to them on the computer.
不要听到后面的“computer”就填上去，那是接收信息的工具，不是让研究领先的核心技术。
In Australia, crocodile studies have been previously conducted by radio. A miniature electronic device was implanted under the skin of these animals...
听到“electronic device”不要急着填，因为题目限制字数，且“radio”才是具体的手段名称。
文中提到在以前的研究（previously conducted）中，鳄鱼研究是通过无线电（radio）进行的。
However, some devices are too old that they always lose signals due to a variety of reasons. So they can't track those animals which they have been studying for months.
你可能想填“data”或“information”，但原文与“lose”直接搭配的词是“signals”。
原文指出旧设备的缺点是太老旧，导致它们总是因为各种原因丢失信号（lose signals）。
But this is a very difficult task because they are alert and afraid of being followed by humans. So it might take the team several hours to capture one.
虽然是“scientists”在抓它们，但原文明确说的害怕对象是“humans”，填空要忠实于原文。
鳄鱼很难捕捉，因为它们很警觉，并且害怕被人类（humans）跟踪。
The tracking device has signal transmitters inside and it's waterproof. It is attached to the head of the crocodile, so the crocodile cannot remove the device with its feet or tail.
注意区分：旧设备是植入“skin”下，新设备是装在“head”上，不要张冠李戴。
新的追踪设备是防水的，并且被安装在鳄鱼的头部（head），这样它们就无法用脚或尾巴弄掉它。
为了控制数量，公园里的科学家必须使用直升机（helicopter）来重新安置鳄鱼。
So scientists at the park have to use a helicopter to relocate the crocodiles in order to control their population in the area.
不要凭借常识填“truck”或“vehicle”，雅思听力必须抓取录音中提到的具体交通工具。
However, scientists found that the relocation methods were ineffective because the relocated crocodiles will return to their original location following the most direct route within one week.
听到“original”不要填，因为它是用来修饰location的，题目问的是修饰route的形容词“direct”。
科学家发现搬迁无效，因为鳄鱼会沿着最直接（direct）的路线在一周内游回原处。
It is interesting to see that they can always find their way and they will not get lost in the ocean. Scientists realized that crocodiles are able to navigate.
题目结构是“ability to...”，后面需要接动词原形，原文中“able to navigate”直接对应答案。
科学家意识到鳄鱼能够总是找到路而不迷失，是因为它们有导航（navigate）的能力。
However, through lots of research and experiments, scientists conclude that crocodiles can tell directions by using their senses to the sun so that they know where they are going.
这里容易走神听到“senses”就以为结束了，答案其实在介词“to”后面的“sun”。
结论显示，鳄鱼通过利用它们对太阳（sun）的感官来辨别方向。
Another finding is that, like the migration of birds who can travel thousands and thousands of kilometers, crocodiles have the same system to help them travel.
千万别填“humans”，原文说的是这是人类不具备（don't possess）的能力，而跟鸟类是相似的。
原文将鳄鱼的迁徙系统与鸟类（birds）进行了类比，指出它们拥有相同的系统。
